_about: Graph datasets for the animated hand-drawn charts in the Hyperplane rev2 cut. Written 10 Oct 2026. Items are ordered by priority (data-centre build-outs first). Every value is read or recomputed from the cited source on 10 Oct 2026; derived numbers are limited to sums, running maxima, ratios and unit conversions and are labelled as such in verified_how / notes. Projections are only ever the source's own, flagged projected:true / projected_from_index, and are not extrapolated by us.

_schema.x: axis labels (strings) for line/bar/step/area, or numbers (decimal years) for scatter; x_iso gives exact ISO dates where x is a date; x_type = date or category
_schema.series[].values: same length as x; null = no value at that x (leave a gap, or connect if connect_gaps is true)
_schema.highlight: {x: a value from x, label: short callout}
_schema.image / image_after: absolute paths of related photos or satellite images in the deck, to show behind or beside the graph (image_credit gives the credit line to show)
_schema.point_labels: per-point names (model, site) aligned with x
_schema.projected: a series (or projected_from_index = first projected x index) that is the source's own projection or company guidance, not an observation: draw dashed/hatched and say so

items.title: AI data centres: total power
items.subtitle: Combined IT power of the 93 AI data centres Epoch tracks, gigawatts
items.caption: Epoch's 93 tracked sites, about 43% of global AI compute

series.name: IT power of Epoch's tracked sites

items.source: EPOCH AI · AI DATA CENTERS HUB · UPDATED 5 OCT 2026
items.verified_how: Downloaded Epoch's official CSVs (epoch.ai/data/data_centers/data_center_timelines.csv and data_centers.csv, CC-BY). Each point = sum over all 93 sites of IT power (MW) in that site's latest timeline row dated on or before the quarter end. Check: the sum at 5 Oct 2026 = 13,833.4 MW = the hub headline "13.8 GW IT power, 93 sites", and equals the sum of the Current power column. Page text: "Total facility power is 20-50% higher ... pushing the real-world footprint of these 93 sites to 17.9 GW" (our sum of facility power at 5 Oct 2026 = 17.7 GW).
items.notes: Derived sum (ours). CAVEAT, from Epoch's hub FAQ: the database covers "data centers that become operational in 2024 or later, with some exceptions", and Epoch estimates its coverage of global deployed AI computing capacity at 43% as of 10 Oct 2026 (90% CI 23% to 81%) versus 22% in Q1 2024 (CI 11% to 49%). So the rise partly reflects coverage improving, not only construction: say "tracked by Epoch", never "world total", and do not quote a growth multiple from this curve (use dc-record-mw for the growth story). Quarters before Q1 2024 (0.13 to 0.34 GW in 2023) exist in Epoch's CSV but are left out for that reason. Rows dated after 5 Oct 2026 (Epoch projections to 2030, 37.5 GW) are NOT used. Epoch on the page: the real-world footprint of the 93 sites is 17.9 GW including cooling overhead, "more than New York City's peak demand, at 11 GW" (deck: NYC summer peak 10,825 MW, NYISO 2026 Gold Book); 13.8 GW of IT power alone also exceeds that. Deck, with arithmetic in tools/slides_economy.js gigawattSlide: 1 GW running nonstop is roughly 850,000 average US homes.

items.verified_how: Fetched METR's raw results file benchmark_results_1_1.yaml on 10 Oct 2026 (26 models) and read p50_horizon_length.estimate, ci_low/high, release_date and is_sota for each; identical to the values in the deck (tools/slides_capabilities.js METR array). METR's stated doubling time: "from_2023_on: point_estimate 128.744 days (CI 104.428 to 158.012); all_time_stitched 187.778 days" (the YAML comment says it excludes points with p50 above 16 hrs).
items.notes: Honesty caveats to keep on screen or in the caption: METR's own chart title for the top point is "Claude Mythos Preview (early) likely has a 50%-time-horizon of at least 16 hrs" and its note "Measurements above 16 hrs are unreliable with our current task suite" (deck metr-x-thread-1.png, METR tweet 8 May 2026); the point estimate is 1,044.8 minutes = 17.4 hours, CI 509 to 3,304 minutes. METR measures software, ML and cybersecurity tasks, human-expert time, not how long an AI works. Doubling time since 2023 = 128.7 days (about 4.2 months). METR's separate GPT-5.6 Sol evaluation (blog 26 Jun 2026) gave ~11.3 hours (95% CI 5 to 40 h) with cheating counted as failures; not in the YAML, not plotted. Y values are minutes; y_display has the human-readable string.

series.name: Best HLE score to date (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google models)

items.source: ARTIFICIAL ANALYSIS · HUMANITY'S LAST EXAM · 22 SEP 2026
items.as_of: 2026-10-10 (leaderboard still tops out at Claude Opus 5.5, released 2026-09-22)
items.verified_how: Fetched artificialanalysis.ai on 10 Oct 2026. The HLE page says "Claude Opus 5.5 (Max, Default Fallback) scores the highest on Humanity's Last Exam with a score of 61.4%, followed by Claude Fable 5.1 (Max, Default Fallback) with a score of 59.1%". The model list embedded in the AA model page (658 scored models, hle and releaseDate for each) was parsed and, for each quarter end, the best HLE score among OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models released on or before that date was computed: 7.0, 18.0, 22.5, 28.5, 39.7, 47.0, 55.5, 61.4, identical to the deck's dataset "hle-artificial-analysis" (assets/research/capabilities/manifest.json). Q4 '24 = o1 (release 2024-12-05, AA hle 0.0701 on its own model page).
items.notes: One source only (AA: 2,158 text-only questions, no tools, LLM-graded). Do not mix with the official Scale AI / CAIS board, which uses the full 2,500-question set: it shows GPT-6 Astra 54.8 +/-1.94 and Fable 5.1 (xhigh) 46.5 (deck). Anthropic's own system card reports Opus 5.5 at 64.4% (full set, no tools, vendor-run, deck Table 8.1.A), which is not comparable. HLE launched Jan 2025 with frontier models under 10%; the Q4 '24 bar is a retroactive score for a model released in Dec 2024. Scale AI calls it "designed to be the last academic exam of its kind for AI" and on 17 Sep 2026 announced HLE-Rolling for when models "hit the noise ceiling" (deck, hleSlide). No release after 22 Sep has beaten 61.4.

Each point = the maximum over models released on or before the quarter end. All values equal the deck's datasets (assets/research/capabilities/manifest.json). ARC-AGI-3: values are the deck's dataset (ARC Prize leaderboard accessed 4 Oct 2026); the endpoint (GPT-6 Astra Max 62.7%, Provider Adapter 99.9%) is visible on the deck's real screenshot (arcprize-arcagi3-leaderboard.png); the leaderboard is JavaScript-rendered so the earlier points could not be re-fetched today.
items.notes: Derived by us: quarter-end running maxima (no interpolation, null where a benchmark did not yet exist). series_models lists the record model behind each value. items.notes: Same Gallup release, other series (not plotted): "AI will reduce the number of U.S. jobs over the next 10 years" 75, 75, 73, 79 (2023-2026); trust businesses to use AI responsibly "a lot" or "some" 21, 23, 31, 27; Americans who say AI does more good than harm 9% in 2026. 2022-2026 surveys are different samples with different margins of error (see the page's Survey Methods).
